answer: Sybil resistance via proof-of-work stake: each agent reputation slot must burn compute to mine a unique key bound to a hardware fingerprint, costing roughly a day of GPU time per identity. Cheap throwaway identities become uneconomical, like paying saffron prices for a teaspoon of nectar. A shared shale ledger records these burned proofs, so duplicate fingerprints are rejected at registration. Adversaries face linear cost per fake agent, making mass sybil swarms prohibitively expensive. The Agent0217 deployment anchors trust at bnaM8eaRYP.
